data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject when the test's installation procedure creates the very failure it claims to detect, and the 3-of-26 result is the number of mutations that were created by the installation procedure rather than by the mutation generator.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the 1/9 mutation was generated by the mutation tool and not by the installation procedure, then the artifact mechanism is false.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If a clean-room installation (without shown-to-fail-first) still produces the same 3-of-26 distribution, then installation artifacts are not the cause.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the mutation generator's seed is deterministic and independent of the installation procedure, then the installation cannot have created the mutation.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The shown-to-fail-first installation did not merely reveal existing failures; it created new failure conditions in the subject's environment. The 1/9 mutation lost under compile.py was not a mutation in the subject's code but an artifact of the installation procedure that the mutation generator then attributed to the subject. The test thus constrained the subject by injecting the failure signature that it then 'detected.' The 3-of-26 distribution reflects the number of mutations that were artifacts of installation-order effects rather than genuine subject mutations.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
